facts.statement: A Markov process is a memoryless stochastic process where only the current value of the variable is relevant for predicting future distributions; historical price paths carry no predictive power.

Standard Wiener Process: Change delta_z across interval delta_t satisfies delta_z = epsilon * sqrt(delta_t) where epsilon ~ N(0, 1), and increments across disjoint intervals are statistically independent.
Generalized Wiener Process: dx = a * dt + b * dz has constant expected drift rate a and constant variance rate b^2. Across finite time T, the change (x_T - x_0) ~ N(a * T, b^2 * T).
Itô Process: Generalized continuous-time process dx = a(x, t) * dt + b(x, t) * dz where drift and variance rate are functions of underlying asset price x and time t.
Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM): Stock price dynamics satisfy dS = mu * S * dt + sigma * S * dz, ensuring percentage returns dS/S are scale-invariant and prices cannot become negative.
Square-Root of Time Dispersion Law: While expected drift accumulates linearly with time t, uncertainty (standard deviation) accumulates with the square root of time sqrt(t).
Path Roughness: Brownian motion sample paths are continuous everywhere but differentiable nowhere, possessing infinite total variation and finite quadratic variation [z, z]_t = t.
Monte Carlo Discrete Propagation: Asset price paths are simulated via S(t + delta_t) = S(t) * [1 + mu * delta_t + sigma * epsilon * sqrt(delta_t)] where epsilon ~ N(0, 1).
